blocking.section: section 5.6, section 4.6, section 14.2; src/borrow.rs::Compiler::compile (qloop arm, lines 363-390) and src/borrow.rs::Evaluation::apply Node::Repeat (lines 694-735)
blocking.problem: Borrowed wires produced inside a plain qloop body are composed as ONE carried wire instead of as fresh borrowed bundles per iteration, so an even trip count falsely proves factorisation. Witness (memoryless, signature kind=perm_action, mut=[1], in=[], mem=[], args=[], bounds=[2]): perm_action @a (t:wire mut) () () () () / regs {  } bounds {2} / ^entry(): / qloop 2 { d = qborrow any 1; cx d t; qreturn d }. After rehashing with the hash command, check exits 0 with status ok (object f349e389...), and run-action --mut 0/1 returns t unchanged only because the executor's default borrow pool is |0>. Hand derivation: iteration i borrows a fresh bundle d_i in an unknown state and applies t ^= d_i, so the operation is t ^= d_0 XOR d_1 with d_0,d_1 independent (choose d_0=1,d_1=0: t flips; with d_i entangled with external references, t becomes correlated with both) - not U_t tensor I on any borrowed bundle. The identical circuit unrolled (two distinct qborrow/cx/qreturn groups) is correctly rejected at hash with 'section 5.6: borrow frame output v0_0 depends on borrowed entry values', as is the single group and the qloop-while form of the same body (which materialises iterations and freshens wires); qloop 4 and nested qloop 2x2 with the same body are also wrongly accepted, and so is 'cx t d' once per iteration over qloop 2 (borrowed bit restored only by cross-iteration aliasing in the proof). Cause: the qborrow arm emits no Node (borrow.rs:312-320), the qloop arm wraps the once-compiled body in Node::Repeat(2,[Flip(d,t)]), and Evaluation::apply for Repeat interns one entry variable for d and squares that body map (borrow.rs:700-730), modelling d as persistent state; a qalloc in the same position is sound only because Node::Alloc resets the wire. Validation therefore depends on loop wrapping, the same soundness class as SOL-R3-B03 but for borrow lifetimes.
blocking.fix: (a) Change src/borrow.rs::Compiler::compile qloop arm and Evaluation::apply/Node::Repeat handling (and Compiler::produce bookkeeping as needed): track the borrowed wires produced while compiling the loop body (including through inlined perm_action children); a body that produces borrowed wires must not be composed by repeated squaring over those wires' single entry variables. (b) Spec: section 5.6 'A region's completed operation equals its declared operation tensor identity on EVERY borrowed bundle' and 'Borrowed wires (set B) are touched ... only inside borrow frames' whose 'realised permutation P_F ... MUST factor as P_F = P' tensor I_B'; section 4.6 'qloop n { body } = body n times'; each execution of the body performs a new qborrow matched by its qreturn (section 5.1 explicit cleanup), so each iteration's frame must factor for its own fresh bundle. (c) Exact expected behaviour: the witness above (and the qloop 4, nested 2x2, and 'cx t d' variants) is rejected at load citing section 5.6 - Object::parse Err and CLI hash/check exit 1 with empty stdout - with no borrow_frames claim in the object; sound implementations either materialise iterations with fresh generation wires like the existing while arm (borrow.rs:365-375) or prove per-iteration factorisation once for body-local borrows (fresh universally-quantified borrowed inputs, outputs equal to those inputs and no influence on carried wires) and then compose only the carried-wire map by squaring; an iteration cap is not acceptable. (d) Test to add in tests/r1_borrow.rs (fails now because check exits 0, passes after): the exact witness plus its unrolled equivalent, both requiring section 5.6 rejection through parser and CLI hash/check; positives that must remain accepted and execute with exact forward/adjoint restoration on every t and every borrowed entry state: (i) borrow outside the loop (d=qborrow; qloop 2 { cx d t }; qreturn d) - one bundle, CX twice; (ii) per-iteration identity body at qloop 2 and at qloop 1099511627776 (d=qborrow; cx d t; cx d t; qreturn d) proving no unrolling/cap was introduced; (iii) extend the generated families in tests/r1_fuzz_discipline.rs with borrows born and returned inside qloop bodies, decided by an independent per-iteration freshness oracle.
